title: Basin-lake resident fauna assemblage
scope: Composition of the basin lake's year-round resident animal community, its lineage sources, and its structural relationship to the spring migrant pulse; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: The lake holds a permanent resident animal community, present year-round and independent of the spring migrant pulses.
Resident aquatic animals are drawn principally from Lineage IV, with Lineage V, VI, and VII members also present.
The bird-like fishing organisms referenced by the spring breeding-pulse record are Lineage III forelimb-winged branch members.
Terrestrial shore hunters are drawn from Lineages I and III.
Residents must survive winter in the lake, including the regular freezing of sheltered bays.
The resident community is structurally dominant: it sets the lake's ecological structure and carries most of its standing animal biomass year-round.
The spring migrant pulse arrives into an already-occupied lake, concentrates in particular places and weeks, and functions as a large seasonal subsidy rather than as the lake's organising force.
The pulse does not restructure the resident community.
boundaries: Resident, shore hunter, and subsidy are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.

Structural dominance describes ecological structure and standing biomass only; it does not downgrade the migrant pulse and establishes no biomass figure, ratio, productivity share, or population number.

The spring breeding-pulse record continues to govern dispersed nursery grounds, shifting feeding grounds, concentrated predators, human harvest activity, migrant-resident competition, adult return and mortality, recruitment variability, and the possibility of exceptional or compound failure, all unchanged.
Lineage assignment is compositional only; it establishes no species, names, taxonomy, resident inventory, sizes, or proportions, and principally fixes no share.

Bird-like continues to describe ecological resemblance only; the Lineage III assignment establishes no feathers, flight performance, Earth-bird anatomy, taxonomy, or named clade beyond the lineage's accepted forelimb-winged branch condition.
Which Lineage IV branches occur, and whether any carry head shields, ion-exchange organs, or gel chambers, remain open; the mass breeder's records continue to govern it alone.
Whether any resident is a Lineage V vault-bearing form remains open; the family-care migrant's records continue to govern it alone.

Winter survival is a requirement placed on residents, not a solution; overwintering behaviour, depth use, torpor, ice tolerance, mortality, and refuge locations remain open, and no deep-water area is established as guaranteed unfrozen.
No resident is established as present at any particular bay, shore, depth, or named place, and none is identified with any harvested, domesticated, or culturally significant animal.
Human fishing practice, seasons, gear, institutions, law, and knowledge remain open; no harvest and no sustainable rate is established.
Reproduction, spawning, diet detail, senses, sociality, disease, parasites, predation rates, and population figures remain open.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, universal creature level, spawn mechanism, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Earth life may inspire author-facing design; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted directly.
Food, oxygen, energy, winter conditions, reproduction, disease, mortality, and carrying capacity remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: The lake is alive year-round, so winter and lean-season scenes have residents in them.
Two-winged Lineage III fishers work the water and Lineage I and III shore hunters work the margins.
The spring pulse lands in an occupied lake rather than an empty one.
Winter conditions rather than summer competition set the resident community's ceiling.
Every species, place, practice, and encounter requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The assemblage describes ordinary community ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, spawn source, refill node, guaranteed harvest, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: Which Lineage IV branches make up the resident aquatic community, and at what sizes?
How do residents overwinter, and where?
Are any residents Lineage V vault-bearing forms?
What do the Lineage III fishers and the Lineage I and III shore hunters actually look like and do?
What year-round harvest, if any, does the settlement take from the resident community?
How does structural dominance resolve under later quantitative productivity modelling?
sources: Author selection and scoping confirmation on 2026-08-17

author_approval.evidence: The Author selected 'C — Resident-dominant lake' from three displayed options on 2026-08-17, then confirmed the scoping 'Residents structure, pulse still major' when the card's marginal-pulse wording was identified as conflicting with the accepted spring-pulse record.
